newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NZ SPORT-NZ offers facilities for Olympic training.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-NZ offers facilities for Olympic training.

text.p: SYDNEY, Nov 4 - Local governments around New Zealand are urging Olympic athletes from around the world to base themselves in places like Wanganui, Gisborne and Dunedin ahead of the Sydney 2000 games, NZPA reported on Monday.
A total of 13 New Zealand city and district councils are included in a 600 page guide to pre-Olympic training released this week by the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games (SOCOG).
The guide lists 90 local government areas and institutions with the capability of hosting teams for training and acclimatisation in the lead-up to the Olympics.
Each section details the weather patterns of the area, landscape, population, sporting facilities, transport and natural attractions.
The 13 New Zealand areas listed are Auckland, Manukau, Hamilton, South Waikato, Rotorua, Gisborne, Hastings, Napier, Wanganui, Palmerston North, Wellington, Christchurch and Dunedin.

Already the United States swimming team has been checking out New Zealand as a base for the 1998 world championships in Sydney, saying New Zealand had advantages because it was outside the mainstream.
President of SOCOG Michael Knight said the guide would be sent to Olympic organisers around the world to let them know what was on offer in Australia and New Zealand.
"To ensure that athletes compete at their best when they actually get to Sydney, they will need good facilities and to be made to feel at home," Knight said.
"I am sure the communities of Australia and New Zealand will engage in a strong competition to put out the welcome mat."
Knight said regions hosting Olympic teams would benefit in terms of business and international exposure.
SOCOG expected teams to visit Australia and New Zealand over the next three years for events, training and acclimatisation with the year leading up to the September 2000 games being the busiest.
